parts.title: Vol 9 Test Passage 1
parts.passageHtml:
Andrew Carnegie: industrialist and philanthropist

The Scottish-born American industrialist and philanthropist Andrew Carnegie, who was the leader of the American steel industry from 1873 to 1901, donated large sums of his fortune to educational, cultural, and scientific institutions. He was born in 1835 in Scotland, the son of William Carnegie, a weaver, and Margaret Morrison Carnegie.

With the invention of weaning machines, William Carnegie’s job disappeared, and eventually the family was forced into poverty. In 1848 the family left Scotland and settled in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in the USA. William found a job in a cotton factory, but he soon quit to return to his home handloom, making linens and trying to sell them door-to-door. Andrew Carnegie also worked in the cotton factory, but after his father died in 1855, his strong desire to help take care of the family pushed him to educate himself. He became an avid reader, a theatergoer, and a lover of music.

Andrew Carnegie became a messenger boy in a telegraph office and later became a telegraph operator. Thomas A. Scott, superintendent of the western division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, made the eighteen-year-old his secretary. Carnegie was soon earning enough to buy a house for his mother. During the Civil War in the United States (1861-65), he helped organize the military telegraph system, but soon returned to Pittsburgh to take Scott’s old job with the railroad.

Between 1865 and 1870 Carnegie made money through investments in several small iron mills and factories. He also traveled throughout England, selling the bonds of small United States railroads and bridge companies. Carnegie began to see that steel was eventually going to replace iron for the manufacture of rails, structural shapes, pipe, and wire. In 1873 he organized a steel rail company and continued building by cutting prices, driving out competitors, shaking off weak partners, and putting earnings back into the company. He never went public (sold shares of his company in order to raise money). Instead he obtained capital from profit, and when necessary from banks, and he kept on growing, making heavy steel alone.

In the 1880s Carnegie’s purchases included a majority stake in the H C Frick Company in Pennsylvania that had vast coal interests, and also the Homestead mills business. Frick became his partner and eventually chairman of the Carnegie Company. Carnegie had moved to New York City in 1867 to be close to the marketing centers for steel products, while Frick stayed in Pennsylvania as the general manager. They made a good team, Behind the scenes, Carnegie planned new projects and the improvement of existing plants; Frick was the working director who watched over the mass-production programs that helped keep price down.

Carnegie spent his leisure time traveling. He also wrote several books, including Triumphant Democracy (1886), which pointed out what he thought were the advantages of life in the United States over the unequal societies of Britain and other European countries. To Carnegie, access to education was the key to America’s political stability and industrial accomplishments. In 1889 he published an article, ‘Wealth’, stating his belief that the rich had a duty to use their money to improve the welfare of the community. Carnegie remained a bachelor until his mother died in 1886. A year Inter he married Louise Whitfield and they had one child together. The couple began to spend six months each year in Scotland, though Carnegie kept an eye on business developments and problems.

Carnegie’s absence from the United States was a factor in the Homestead mills strike of 1892. After acquiring Homestead, Carnegie had invested in new plants and equipment, increased production, and automated many of the mill’s operations, cutting down the number of workers that were needed. Carnegie believed that workers had a right to join unions and to bargain with management through their unions. He also recognized the right to strike, as long as the action was conducted peacefully. He viewed strikes as trials of strength, with peaceful discussion resolving the conflict. In contract talks during 1892, Frick wanted to lower the minimum wage because of the need for fewer workers. The union representing his workers would not accept this and organized a strike.

Following a violent confrontation that resulted in the death of eight workers, soldiers were sent in to restore order and Carnegie was criticized for his lack of action. In the 1890s Carnegie also began to meet with tougher competition from newer, bigger companies who were interested in controlled prices and sharing the market. Companies that he had sold to for years threatened to cut down their purchases unless be agreed to cooperate. These threats made him decide to fight back. He refused to enter into any agreements with other companies. Moreover, he decided to invade their territories by making similar products and by expanding his sales activities into the west of the country. Eventually, though, he decided to sell his company to the newly formed U.S. Steel Corporation in 1901 for almost $500 million. Carnegie’s personal share was $225 million.

In retirement, Carnegie began to set up trust funds ‘for the improvement of mankind’. He built some three thousand public libraries all over the English-speaking world and funded galleries, museums and concert halls in the US. He also built a group of technical schools, a research institute, and a foundation providing pensions for university professors. When Carnegie died in 1919, the continuation of his broad interests was put under the general charge of the Carnegie Corporation, with a donation of $125 million.

questions.text: 1835-1855 • found employment in the same workplace as his 1_____________ • educated himself through books, theatrical performances and 2_____________
questions.explanationHtml:
1. father

Câu hỏi: found employment In the same workplace as his ______

(Có việc làm ở cùng nơi làm việc với ______ của anh ấy.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Andrew Carnegie also worked in the cotton factory, but after his father died in 1855, his strong desire to help take care of the family pushed him to educate himself.

(Andrew Carnegie cũng làm việc trong nhà máy bông, nhưng sau khi cha của ông mất vào năm 1855, mong muốn chăm sóc gia đình mãnh liệt của ông đã thúc đẩy ông tự học.)

questions.text: 1835-1855 • found employment in the same workplace as his 1_____________ • educated himself through books, theatrical performances and 2_____________
questions.explanationHtml:
2. music

Câu hỏi: educated himself through books, theatrical performances and ______

(Tự học thông qua sách, các buổi biểu diễn sân khấu và ______.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

He became an avid reader, a theatergoer, and a lover of music.

(Ông trở thành người đọc sách say mê, người xem kịch, và một người yêu âm nhạc.)

questions.text: 1855-1865 • worked in a telegraph office • became 3_____________ to Thomas A Scott at Pennsylvania Railroad
questions.explanationHtml:
3. secretary

Câu hỏi: became_______ to Thomas A Scott at Pennsylvania Railroad

(Trở thành ______ của Thomas A. Scott tại Pennsylvania Railroad.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Scott, superintendent of the western division of the Pennsylvania Railroad, made the eighteen-year-old his secretary.

(Scott, giám đốc khu vực phía tây của đường ray Pennsylvania, đã bổ nhiệm chàng trai 18 tuổi làm thư ký của mình.)

questions.text: 1865-1870 • made investments in the US and England • realised that changing engineering needs would require a greater demand for 4_____________
questions.explanationHtml:
4. steel

Câu hỏi: realised that changing engineering needs would require a greater demand for ______

(Nhận ra rằng nhu cầu kỹ thuật thay đổi sẽ cần nhu cầu lớn hơn về ______.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Carnegie began to see that steel was eventually going to replace iron for the manufacture of rails, structural shapes, pipe, and wire.

(Carnegie bắt đầu thấy rằng thép sẽ cuối cùng thay thế sắt trong sản xuất đường ray, cấu kiện kết cấu, ống, và dây điện.)

questions.text: 1873 • managed a rail manufacturing business by: + reducing 5_____________ + restructuring + reinvesting profit and sometimes borrowing money from 6_____________
questions.explanationHtml:
5. prices

Câu hỏi: managed a rail manufacturing business by: reducing_____

(quản lý một doanh nghiệp sản xuất đường ray bằng cách: giảm _____)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

In 1873 he organized a steel rail company and continued building by cutting prices, driving out competitors, shaking off weak partners, and putting earnings back into the company.

(Vào năm 1873, ông thành lập một công ty đường sắt thép và tiếp tục phát triển nó bằng cách giảm giá thành, loại bỏ các đối thủ cạnh tranh, chấm dứt kinh doanh với các đối tác yếu, và tái đầu tư lợi nhuận vào công ty.)

questions.text: 1873 • managed a rail manufacturing business by: + reducing 5_____________ + restructuring + reinvesting profit and sometimes borrowing money from 6_____________
questions.explanationHtml:
6. banks

Câu hỏi: reinvesting profit and sometimes borrowing money from ________

(tái đầu tư lợi nhuận và đôi khi vay tiền từ ______)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

He never went public (sold shares of his company in order to raise money). Instead he obtained capital from profit, and when necessary from banks, and he kept on growing, making heavy steel alone.

(Ông ấy chưa bao giờ niêm yết cổ phiếu công ty để huy động vốn. Thay vào đó, ông ấy lấy vốn từ lợi nhuận, và khi cần thiết thì vay từ ngân hàng, và tiếp tục phát triển, chỉ chuyên sản xuất thép nặng.)

questions.text: 1880s • Frick and Carnegie became partners • Carnegie’s responsibilities: + arranging future 7_____________ and innovations for factories • Frick's responsibilities: Production
questions.explanationHtml:
7. projects

Câu hỏi: arranging future ________ and innovations for factories

(sắp xếp các ______ và cải tiến trong tương lai cho các nhà máy.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

They made a good team, Behind the scenes, Carnegie planned new projects and the improvement of existing plants

(Họ là một đội ăn ý. Sau hậu trường, Carnegie lên kế hoạch cho các dự án mới và cải tiến các nhà máy hiện có.)

questions.text: 8 Carnegie believed that the USA offered more opportunities than European countries did.
questions.explanationHtml:
8. True

Câu hỏi: Carnegie believed that the USA offered more opportunities than European countries did.

(Carnegie tin rằng Mỹ mang lại nhiều cơ hội hơn các nước châu Âu.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

He also wrote several books, including Triumphant Democracy (1886), which pointed out what he thought were the advantages of life in the United States over the unequal societies of Britain and other European countries.

(Ông cũng viết một số cuốn sách, trong đó có cuốn "Nền Dân Chủ Chiến Thắng" (1886), chỉ ra những gì ông cho là lợi thế của cuộc sống ở Hoa Kỳ so với các xã hội bất bình đẳng của Anh và các nước châu Âu khác.)

Giải thích: Câu này chữ “opportunities” và chữ “advantages of life” có thể hiểu gần giống nhau nên True.

questions.text: 9 A smaller workforce was required at the Homestead factory after Carnegie took control.
questions.explanationHtml:
9. True

Câu hỏi: A smaller workforce was required at the Homestead factory after Carnegie took control.

(Sau khi Carnegie tiếp quản nhà máy Homestead, số lượng công nhân cần thiết giảm đi.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

After acquiring Homestead, Carnegie had invested in new plants and equipment, increased production, and automated many of the mill’s operations, cutting down the number of workers that were needed.

(Sau khi mua Homestead, Carnegie đã đầu tư vào các nhà máy và thiết bị mới, tăng sản lượng và tự động hóa nhiều công đoạn của nhà máy, giảm số lượng công nhân cần thiết.)

Giải thích: “cutting down the number of workers” = cần ít lao động hơn.

questions.text: 10 Carnegie prevented his workers from joining unions.
questions.explanationHtml:
10. False

Câu hỏi: Carnegie prevented his workers from joining unions.

(Carnegie ngăn công nhân tham gia công đoàn.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Carnegie believed that workers had a right to join unions and to bargain with management through their unions.

(Carnegie tin rằng người công nhân có quyền gia nhập công đoàn và thương lượng với ban quản lý thông qua công đoàn của họ.)

Giải thích: ông ủng hộ chứ không ngăn cản

questions.text: 11 Carnegie blamed Frick for the violent workers strike in 1892.
questions.explanationHtml:
11. NG

Câu hỏi: Carnegie blamed Frick for the violent workers strike in 1892.

(Carnegie đổ lỗi cho Frick về cuộc đình công bạo lực năm 1892.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

Following a violent confrontation that resulted in the death of eight workers, soldiers were sent in to restore order and Carnegie was criticized for his lack of action.

(Sau một cuộc đối đầu bạo lực khiến tám công nhân thiệt mạng, binh lính đã được điều đến để lập lại trật tự và Carnegie bị chỉ trích vì thiếu hành động.)

Giải thích: Bài chỉ nói Carnegie bị chỉ trích, không nói ông đổ lỗi cho Frick.

questions.text: 12 In the 1890s Carnegie negotiated with his competitors.
questions.explanationHtml:
12. False

Câu hỏi: In the 1890s Carnegie negotiated with his competitors.

(Trong những năm 1890, Carnegie thương lượng với các đối thủ cạnh tranh.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

In the 1890s Carnegie also began to meet with tougher competition from newer, bigger companies who were interested in controlled prices and sharing the market. Companies that he had sold to for years threatened to cut down their purchases unless be agreed to cooperate. These threats made him decide to fight back. He refused to enter into any agreements with other companies.

(Vào những năm 1890, Carnegie cũng bắt đầu phải đối mặt với sự cạnh tranh gay gắt hơn từ các công ty mới hơn, lớn hơn quan tâm đến việc kiểm soát giá cả và chia sẻ thị trường.Các công ty mà ông đã bán hàng cho trong nhiều năm đe dọa sẽ giảm lượng mua nếu ông không đồng ý hợp tác. Những lời đe dọa này khiến ông quyết định chống trả. Ông từ chối ký kết bất kỳ thỏa thuận nào với các công ty khác.)

• Bẫy ở đây "negotiate" dễ bị nhầm là meet with, nhưng ở đây là meet with tougher competition là “đối mặt với cạnh tranh mạnh mẽ hơn” nên key nằm ở câu dưới: He refused to enter into any agreements with other companies. => False

questions.text: 13 Carriage’s provision of funds for libraries was limited to those in the United States.
questions.explanationHtml:
13. False

Câu hỏi: Carnegie’s provision of funds for libraries was limited to those in the United States.

(Việc Carnegie tài trợ cho thư viện chỉ giới hạn ở Mỹ.)

Đoạn chứa đáp án:

He built some three thousand public libraries all over the English-speaking world and funded galleries, museums and concert halls in the US.

(Ông đã xây dựng khoảng ba nghìn thư viện công cộng trên khắp thế giới nói tiếng Anh và tài trợ cho các phòng trưng bày, bảo tàng và phòng hòa nhạc ở Hoa Kỳ.)

Giải thích: Các thư viện không chỉ ở Mỹ mà ở toàn bộ thế giới nói tiếng Anh.
